chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar al-Hamdani — all of them from al-Fath ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the lowest of recognition. So he said: 'The acknowledgement that there is no god other than Him, and there is no resemblance for Him, and no counterpart, and that He is eternal, affirmed, existent without being absent, and that there is nothing like unto Him.'

key_terms.أدنى المعرفة: The lowest/minimum level of divine recognition — the foundational acknowledgement required of every believer
key_terms.الإقرار: Acknowledgement, affirmation, confession — an active verbal and intellectual act of recognition
key_terms.قديم: Pre-eternal, having no beginning — a core divine attribute in Shia kalam theology
key_terms.ليس كمثله شيء: There is nothing like unto Him — echoing Quran 42:11, the foundational verse of divine incomparability
key_terms.موجود غير فقيد: Existent without being absent — affirming God's continuous and active presence

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum level of recognition of God according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), likely Imam al-Ridha (AS), defines the minimum threshold of divine recognition (ma'rifa): affirming God's absolute oneness (tawhid), His incomparability, His eternity, and His continuous presence — culminating in the Quranic declaration that nothing is like Him. This teaching was given to al-Fath ibn Yazid, one of the Imam's trusted companions, who sought to understand the foundational requirement of faith. The phrase 'كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ' directly echoes Quran 42:11, grounding theological inquiry in scripture.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Abdullah Bin Al Hassan Al Alary, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Al Mukhtar Bin Muhammad Bin Al Mukhtar Al Hamdany, altogether from Al Fatah Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the lowest of the recognition. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The acknowledgement that there is no god apart from Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is neither a resemblance for Him<sup>azwj</sup> nor a counterpart, and that He<sup>azwj</sup> is Eternal, Affirmed, Existing without being absent, and that there is nothing like Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn al- Hassan has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Hassan al-‘Alawi and Ali ibn Ibrahim from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar al-Hmadini altogether from al- Fath ibn Yazid who has said the following.

“I asked Imam abul Hassan (a.s.), “What is the minimum required degree of knowledge about Allah?” The Imam said, “To acknowledge that there is no other lord besides Him and that nothing is similar to and like Him and that He is eternal, positively existing and not absence and that nothing is like Him.”
